rv.q: Douglas Carter Beane's comedy about a movie star in the closet and his scheming agent is smart, funny and surprisingly touching.
Her delivery of Mr. Beane’s dialogue ensures that theatergoers who thought that wit that both sings and stings would never echo again on Broadway without a British accent have cause to rejoice.
Almost everyone thinks Beane's satire about closeted gay Hollywood is cutting-edge funny. Wish I could, too.
Planted firmly in the driver’s seat Julie White puts the medal to the pedal for an adrenaline spiked ride that is a laughed filled delight.
